texts.preamble: Ashok Kumar vs Mukesh Sah on 24 February, 2025 In The Court Of Ms. Charu Gupta Presiding Officer, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-01 (Se), Saket Courts : New Delhi Mact No: 645/2021 Ashok Kumar vs. Mukesh Sah & anr. Cnr No: Dlse01-0088902021 1. Ashok Kumar @ Ashok Singh S/o Chandrika Singh R/o Village & Post Barahi Jagdish Ps Purnahiya, Distt. Sheohar, Bihar.
texts.facts: The brief facts of the case are that on 28.11.2019 at about 07:30 a.m. petitioner along with his friend Arvind Pandey was traveling from Ayodhya to Gorakhpur in vehicle TATA Ace bearing no.UP-53BT-6001 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle). The offending vehicle was being driven at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner. When offending vehicle reached Bihar Mod, NH-28, it hit into another vehicle bearing no. UP-71AT-3371. Due to the forceful impact, the offending vehicle in which petitioner was traveling turned turtle causing grievous injury to the petitioner and other occupants. Petitioner was taken to Sadar Hospital, Basti U.P. for treatment and was later referred to AIIMS Hospital, Patna for further treatment. While petitioner sustained permanent disability on account of the injury, his friend Arvind Pandey lost his life. 3. An FIR no.0255/2019 was registered u/s 279/337/338 of MACT No.645/21 Ashok Kumar vs. Mukesh Sah & anr. P.No. 2 of 25 ss Digitally signed by CHARU CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.02.24 04:45:44 +0530 IPC against respondent no.1. Upon investigation chargesheet, was filed before concerned criminal court and a claim petition was filed before this Tribunal. 4. Respondent no.1 is the driver cum owner and respondent no.2 is the insurance company with which such offending vehicle was insured. 5. In response to the claim petition, respondent no.1 filed his reply denying negligence or fault on his part in committing the accident. He has pleaded that it was the petitioner and other passengers who insisted respondent no.1 to drive at a speed as they were getting late. It is further pleaded that another vehicle no.UP-71AT-3371 suddenly applied brakes. In order to avert greater harm, respondent no.1 also applied brakes as a result of which both the vehicles collided and petitioner got injured. It is further pleaded that the offending vehicle was duly insured with respondent no.2. In its reply, respondent no.2/insurance company has challenged the territorial jurisdiction of this Tribunal as the accident took place within the territory of U.P., petitioner as well as respondent no.1 are permanent residents of U.P. while the office from which the insurance policy has been issued is situated at Jaipur, Rajasthan. Respondent no.2 has also pleaded that the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties and that impleading of driver of vehicle no. UP-71AT-3371 was necessary for proper adjudication of the matter. It is further pleaded that the petitioner was traveling as an unauthorized passenger in a goods carrying vehicle and therefore respondent no.1 who allowed petitioner to MACT No.645/21 Ashok Kumar vs. Mukesh Sah & anr. P.No. 3 of 25 ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2025.02.24 04:45:48 +0530 ply in his vehicle is solely responsible to compensate. Issuance of insurance policy to the offending vehicle is however not disputed. After completion of pleadings, following issues were framed on 02.02.2024. 1. OPP. 3. Relief. 7. Thereafter, evidence was led by the petitioner by examining himself as PW-1. PW-1/petitioner Ashok Kumar @ Ashok Singh tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A wherein he testified on the lines of his claim petition. He also relied upon documents i.e. copy of FIR as Ex.PW1/A (colly), certified copy of chargesheet as Ex.PW1/B (colly), certified copy of release documents of vehicle as Ex.PW1/C, copy of Bail Bond as Ex.PW/1D, copy of undertaking as Ex.PW1/E, original medical bills as Ex.PW1/F (colly), Disability certificate as Ex.PW1/F, Adahar Card as Ex.PW1/G and Voter ID Card as Ex.PW1/G. PW-1 was duly cross examined by Ld. Counsel for insurance company. In respondent evidence, respondent no.2/insurance company examined. RW-1/Sh. Nishant Tripathi, Sr. Legal Executive at Shri Ram MACT No.645/21 Ashok Kumar vs. Mukesh Sah & anr. P.No. 4 of 25 ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2025.02.24 04:45:52 +0530 General Insurance company. RW1 has tendered the evidence by way of affidavit. He relied upon copy of affidavit as Ex.R3W1/1 (colly), copy of insurance policy as Ex.R3W1/2 (colly) and copy of postal receipt as Ex.R3W4/4. RW1 has been cross examined by Ld. Counsel for petitioner and ld. counsel for driver cum owner.

(2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ Ashok Kumar vs Mukesh Sah on 24 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158005794/ 3 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. 10. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the MACT No.645/21 Ashok Kumar vs. Mukesh Sah & anr. P.No. 6 of 25 ss CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.02.24 04:45:59 +0530 offending vehicle. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. However in view of judgment of Malti Sardar vs. NIC, there is no bar to a claim petition being filed at a place where the insurance company, which is the main contesting Ashok Kumar vs Mukesh Sah on 24 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158005794/ 4 party, has its business. Thus, the plea of lack of Territorial Jurisdiction is unsustainable. Respondent no.2 has further raised a defence of non joinder of owner/driver/insurance company of vehicle no. UP-71AT-3371 as redering the claim petition bad in law. This argument of respondent no.2 is unsustainable in MACT No.645/21 Ashok Kumar vs. Mukesh Sah & anr. P.No. 7 of 25 ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2025.02.24 04:46:03 +0530 the light of settled legal principle as per which claimant is considered to be dominus litis/ master of his case and it is his discretion to array the parties as respondents. It has been held in Shree Ram General Insurance company v. Meena Uppal CM(M) 1221229/2016 decided on 29.04.2024, wherein Hon'bl;e Delhi High Court observed that even in the case of contributory negligence or for that matter composite negligence, the liability of the joint tort feasor i.e. the driver and the registered owner of the offending vehicle shall not stand diluted and their liability would be joint and several and the insurance company is liable to indemnify the insured. As regards the issue of liability of the respondents, respondent no.2 has raised a statutory defence pleading that the offending vehicle was being plied in breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy in as much as the offending vehicle held a registration certificate of a goods carriage vehicle and was not permitted to carry the petitioner as a passenger. It is MACT No.645/21 Ashok Kumar vs. Mukesh Sah & anr. P.No. 8 of 25 ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.02.24 04:46:10 +0530 further pleaded that since the petitioner was merely a gratuitous passenger traveling in the offending vehicle without authorization, insurance company is not liable to compensate him. In order to establish his defence respondent no.2 has examined Sh. Nishant Tripathi, Sr. Legal Executive as RW1. RW1 has duly proved the terms and conditions of the insurance policy which clearly do not cover the use of offending vehicle as a passenger vehicle. Perusal of the policy and RC of vehicle establish that the offending vehicle was carrying the victims as gratuitous passengers and as such, there is certainly a breach of the terms and conditions of insurance policy. Now, whether the payment of compensation is to made jointly by the owner cum driver of the vehicle or by the insurer which could thereafter be recovered from such owner /driver, has to be considered in the light of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Ashok Kumar vs Mukesh Sah on 24 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158005794/ 5 Court in Anu Bhanvara vs. IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Company AIR 2019 SC 3934. In the said judgment, Apex Court held that the insurance of the vehicle, though as a goods vehicle, is not disputed by the parties. It held that since the claimants were young children who suffered permanent disability on account of the injuries sustained in the accident, the principle of "pay and recover" should be directed to be invoked in the present case. The court accordingly held that the insurance company shall have right to realize the compensation amount from the driver and owner of the vehicle in accordance with the law. Reliance is also placed on decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Manuara Khatoon vs. Rajesh Kumar Singh AIR 2017 MACT No.645/21 Ashok Kumar vs. Mukesh Sah & anr. P.No . 9 of 25 wherein the court while referring to the case of Manager, National Insurance company Ltd. vs. Saju P. Paul & anr. (2013) 2SCC observed : "...16. This question also fell for consideration recently in Manager, National Insurance Company Limited vs. Saju P. Paul & Anr., (supra) wherein this Court took note of entire previous case law on the subject mentioned above and examined the question in the context of Section 147 of the Act. While allowing the appeal filed by the Insurance Company by reversing the judgment of the High Court, it was held on facts that since the victim was travelling in offending vehicle as "gratuitous passenger" and hence, the Insurance Company cannot be held liable to suffer the liability arising out of accident on the strength of the insurance policy. 17. Justice R.M. Lodha (as His Lordship then was and later became CJI) speaking for the Bench held in paras 20 and 26 as under: "20. The recovery of the amount by the Insurance Company from the owner shall be made by following the procedure as laid down by this Court in Challa Upendra Rao (supra)..." and it was further observed in para "... 22. Further it is noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the MACT No.645/21 Ashok Kumar vs. Mukesh Sah & anr.
